hard_requirements: Target cells = cells blank in input.xlsx and filled in golden.xlsx.
Input identical to golden outside the targets (no planted hardcodes, no edits).
Every golden target is a live formula (golden passes its own formula-coverage check), except tier-B cells the golden fixes at 0.
Every golden target formula traces through formulas to numeric input constants; no circular references, no direct references to empty cells.
Golden has cached values for every target; no error values.
No iterative (IRR/XIRR/RATE) or volatile functions in the target chain.
Assumptions used by golden formulas exist as input cells or are stated on the sheet (e.g. '3% of EGR' in a label, 'use 90 days' note).
Final output has a non-zero value and responds to an input change.
criteria.verification: Every selected golden was recalculated in Microsoft Excel (COM); all target values matched the cached values, and a +10% change to one input changed the final output (recorded in case.json).

other_categories.Visualization: Excluded: 24 chart-creation tasks graded by rubric, not formula models.
other_categories.Debugging: Excluded: 100 'audit and fix this file' tasks on large multi-sheet workbooks; the target is repairing existing cells, not building a formula chain from blanks.

Financial_Model.decision: Deferred, not rejected: 100 tasks over 20 full multi-sheet models (5 input variants share one golden). Some are structurally clean (e.g. 01_01, 15_04: all blank targets are formulas, no other diffs), but they have 8-25 sheets, thousands of formulas, targets spread across sheets and long multi-part instructions (3 of 100 ask for a hardcoded value). Good candidates for a later 'hard' tier once the evaluator handles multi-sheet models; too large for the first flow.
Financial_Model.note: A full dependency-trace scan of this category was started and stopped: too slow on models of this size. The sample above is a plain input-vs-golden diff.
